newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indofood says acquisition price now lower.
newsitem.headline: Indofood says acquisition price now lower.

text.p: Indonesian noodle-maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur said on Tuesday that the price of a planned series of acquisitions of sister companies has dropped to 1.55 trillion rupiah from the previous 1.75 trillion rupiah.
The company said in a statement that the price was reduced "to give more value to public shareholders".

The company said also that the rights issue which will partly fund the acquisitions has been accordingly amended. The rights offering will be at a ratio of five shares to each one held from the previous 4:1 ratio. The shares will be offered at a price of 3,300 rupiah each, it said.
The acquisition plan, under which Indofood was to acquire six units of the Salim Group, of which it is also a member, has drawn some adverse reactions.
Analysts have said the plan does not offer shareholders tangible benefits and had said the previous 1.75 trillion rupiah price was too high. There was no immediate reaction to the new plan.
The companies to be acquired include firms in the oil palm plantations business, a cooking oil producer and a palm oil trader.
Indofood also said that the acquisition plan would be presented to a shareholders meeting on April 3. The meeting was previously scheduled for March 17.
Indofood closed at 5,600 rupiah on the Jakarta bourse on Tuesday, up 200.
